gloss: butterbur bud; butterbur flower stalk (early-spring wild vegetable)

definitions.gloss: butterbur bud; the young flower stalk of the butterbur
definitions.explanation: The pale green bud that pushes up from the ground before the butterbur's leaves appear. Prized as one of the first wild vegetables of the year and known for its strong bitterness.

examples.japanese: ふきのとう⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{天|てん}ぷら→天ぷら：04948_tenpura⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{苦|にが}い→苦い：01201_nigai⟧。

examples.english: Butterbur buds were poking up on the embankment.
When the snow melts, butterbur buds sprout and let us know that spring has come.

notes:
Written {蕗|ふき}の{薹|とう} in kanji, but normally kana. Literally 'the {薹|とう} (flower stalk) of the ⟦{蕗|ふき}→蕗：30515_fuki⟧ (butterbur).' A standard image of early spring in haiku and in seasonal cooking.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ふきのとう⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{天|てん}ぷら→天ぷら：04948_tenpura⟧: butterbur bud tempura
- ふきのとう⟦{味噌|みそ}→味噌：01037_miso⟧: butterbur bud miso
- ふきのとう⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{芽|め}→芽：02141_me⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{出|だ}す→出す：01087_dasu⟧: butterbur buds sprout
- ふきのとう⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{摘|つ}む→摘む：02472_tsumu⟧: to pick butterbur buds

USAGE:
Because the bitterness is the point, ふきのとう is cooked in ways that keep it: tempura, or chopped into miso. The related word ⟦{蕗|ふき}→蕗：30515_fuki⟧ refers to the leaf stalks, which are eaten later in spring and taste much milder.

- ⟦{筍|たけのこ}→筍：17667_takenoko⟧: bamboo shoot — the other famous early-spring vegetable, sweet rather than bitter
